title: dbBind rejects ADBC schemas with empty positional parameter names
description:
ADBC requires empty field names for unnamed parameters. adbi 0.1.3 and upstream `ac5d3294597c453c8cb1c278b9536cd9afb3eae2` (version 0.1.4 in DESCRIPTION) treat these as named placeholders, rejecting positional `dbBind()` with `Expecting named params for named placeholders`.

Reproduce against the native Redis ADBC driver:

```r
library(DBI)
library(adbi)
driver <- adbcdrivermanager::adbc_driver(Sys.getenv("REDIS_ADBC_LIBRARY"))
con <- dbConnect(adbi(driver), uri = Sys.getenv("REDIS_URI"))
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT CAST(? AS INTEGER) AS value")
schema <- nanoarrow::nanoarrow_schema_parse(
  adbcdrivermanager::adbc_statement_get_parameter_schema(res@statement), recursive = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(names(schema$children), ""))
dbBind(res, list(2L))
stopifnot(dbFetch(res)$value == 2L)
dbClearResult(res)
dbDisconnect(con)
```

The positional metadata follows the [ADBC contract](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/20/cpp/api/group__adbc-statement.html): unnamed parameters have empty field names. `named_schema` currently compares names only to numeric and `$n` conventions; an empty name passes both inequalities. `dbBindArrow()` delegates to the same check in the installed package, so it does not provide a workaround.

## Proposed fix

In `R/dbBind_AdbiResult.R`:

```diff
     named_schema <- all(
-      names(schema) != as.character(seq_along(schema) - 1L) &
+      nzchar(names(schema)) &
+        names(schema) != as.character(seq_along(schema) - 1L) &
         names(schema) != paste0("$", seq_along(schema))
     )
```

Proposed regression to append to `tests/testthat/test-parameters.R` (using its existing helper):

```r
test_that("empty field names denote positional parameters", {
  driver <- local_parameter_connection(metadata = TRUE)
  original <- get_parameter_schema
  local_mocked_bindings(get_parameter_schema = function(statement) {
    schema <- original(statement)
    names(schema$children) <- rep("", length(schema$children))
    schema
  })
  res <- dbSendQuery(driver$con, "SELECT ? AS x, ? AS y")
  expect_error(dbBind(res, list(x = 1L, y = 2L)), "unnamed")
  expect_error(dbBind(res, list(1L)), "equally many")
  dbBind(res, list(1L, NA_integer_))
  expect_equal(dbFetch(res), data.frame(x = 1L, y = NA_integer_))
  dbBind(res, list(3L, 4L))
  expect_equal(dbFetch(res), data.frame(x = 3L, y = 4L))
  dbClearResult(res)
})
```

## Validation

Four real Redis integration cases check integer filtering, multiple integer parameters, NULL text, mixed NULL/integer values and rebinding. They assert empty schema field names before binding. All four fail with unpatched upstream and pass with an isolated installation of that same upstream source plus the proposed fix. The native read test also passes; the Redis driver schema was unchanged. The proposed testthat regression above has not been run in the full upstream package suite.

Environment: macOS arm64, R 4.6.2, DBI 1.3.0, adbcdrivermanager 0.25.0, nanoarrow 0.9.0; Redis Software 8.6.2, Search, verified active 4x QPF.

Local tracker: https://github.com/redis/redis-adbc-driver/issues/252

Prepared with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex).

title: Strict `bigint` modes re-signal the conversion warning instead of raising an error
description:
In a strict `bigint` mode, such as the default `integer-strict`, a 64-bit value that does not fit is meant to fail the conversion. The condition it raises is nanoarrow's warning, though, so an error handler does not see it, and muffling warnings turns the value into `NA`:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
tryCatch(
  dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 10000000000 AS a"),
  error = function(e) "error",
  warning = function(w) class(w)[[1L]]
)
#> [1] "nanoarrow_warning_lossy_conversion"
suppressWarnings(dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 10000000000 AS a"))
#>    a
#> 1 NA
```

The strict handler passes the warning to `stop()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/dbFetch_AdbiResult.R#L226-L229)), which signals a condition object with its own class. A handler that muffles warnings, as `suppressWarnings()` and testthat do, then resumes the conversion through the `muffleWarning` restart of nanoarrow's `warning()` call, which is still active. This is also why DBItest's 64-bit tests see `NA` rather than an error.

With `stop(conditionMessage(w), call. = FALSE)` instead, on a copy of `main`, the `tryCatch()` above returns `"error"`, the `suppressWarnings()` call fails, and the test suite still passes.

title: A deferred `dbDisconnect()` runs again when a result is cleared a second time
description:
Clearing a result a second time after a deferred `dbDisconnect()` has closed the connection runs the deferred close again. Next to the warning that the DBI specification asks for ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBItest/blob/2483a47ce020ac3a4de0bcd42e58383a777bb065/R/spec-result-clear-result.R#L37-L43)), the second clear then warns that the connection and the database are already released:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT 1")
dbDisconnect(con)
#> There are 1 result(s) in use. The connection will be released when they are closed
dbClearResult(res)
dbClearResult(res)
#> Warning: Statement already released.
#> Warning: Connection already closed.
#> Warning: Database already released.
```

The deferred close is the check at the end of `rm_result()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/fe650e5bc6579b2fdb5791f5970b3304454fcfc5/R/utils.R#L52-L57)), which calls `dbDisconnect()` while the connection is marked for closing and has no results left. The `dbClearResult()` method calls `rm_result()` for a result it has already cleared too, after its warning ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/fe650e5bc6579b2fdb5791f5970b3304454fcfc5/R/dbClearResult_AdbiResult.R#L11-L17)), and the flag that marks the connection outlives the close: the deferred branch of `dbDisconnect()` sets it ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/fe650e5bc6579b2fdb5791f5970b3304454fcfc5/R/dbDisconnect_AdbiConnection.R#L34)), and nothing unsets it when the connection is released ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/fe650e5bc6579b2fdb5791f5970b3304454fcfc5/R/dbDisconnect_AdbiConnection.R#L39-L49)). A forced `dbDisconnect()` after a deferred one leaves it set as well, so clearing one of the results it cleared warns the same way.

Unsetting the flag where `dbDisconnect()` releases the connection consumes it on every path that closes the connection:

```r
    return(invisible(FALSE))
  }

  meta(conn, "disconnect") <- FALSE

  if (adbc_connection_is_valid(conn@connection)) {
```

With that, the second clear warns only that the statement is already released, after a deferred close and after a forced one, both on `main` and with the fix for #120, and the test suite passes either way. Unsetting the flag in `rm_result()` instead, ahead of the deferred close, would not cover the forced close once #120 is fixed, since that fix restores the flag before the forced close releases the connection.

title: A deferred `dbDisconnect()` fires inside a forced close or the next query
description:
A `dbDisconnect()` that is deferred because results are open runs once the last of them is cleared. It also runs when adbi clears them itself with `clear_results()`, as a forced close does, and as each new query does under `options(adbi.allow_multiple_results = FALSE)`. A forced close after a deferred one then finds the connection and the database already released:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT 1")
dbDisconnect(con)
#> There are 1 result(s) in use. The connection will be released when they are closed
dbDisconnect(con, force = TRUE)
#> Warning in .local(conn, ...): There are 1 open result(s) in use. Force closing
#> can be disabled by setting `options(adbi.force_close_results = FALSE)`.
#> Warning: Connection already closed.
#> Warning: Database already released.
```

The deferred close is the check at the end of `rm_result()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/edb08fc340b645bc3923493f13515804dda94d7c/R/utils.R#L60-L62)), which calls `dbDisconnect()` once the connection is marked for closing and has no results left. The forced branch of `dbDisconnect()` clears the results with `clear_results()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/edb08fc340b645bc3923493f13515804dda94d7c/R/dbDisconnect_AdbiConnection.R#L17-L25)), so clearing the last one releases the connection and the database before the forced branch tries to release them itself ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/edb08fc340b645bc3923493f13515804dda94d7c/R/dbDisconnect_AdbiConnection.R#L39-L49)). The connection still ends up closed and the call returns `TRUE`; only the two warnings are wrong.

Under the single-result policy, the next query's statement is already open ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/edb08fc340b645bc3923493f13515804dda94d7c/R/AdbiResult.R#L54-L90)) when `register_result()` clears the other results ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/edb08fc340b645bc3923493f13515804dda94d7c/R/utils.R#L23-L34)), so the deferred close fires with it open and both releases fail:

```r
options(adbi.allow_multiple_results = FALSE)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
res1 <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT 1")
dbDisconnect(con)
#> There are 1 result(s) in use. The connection will be released when they are closed
res2 <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT 2")
#> Warning in register_result(connection, res): Open result(s) already exists for
#> this connection and will be closed. To enable multiple open results, set
#> `options(adbi.allow_multiple_results = TRUE)`.
#> <adbcsqlite_connection/adbc_connection/adbc_xptr> has 1 unreleased child object
#> <adbcsqlite_database/adbc_database/adbc_xptr> has 1 unreleased child object
```

The connection stays open, then, and closes once `res2` is cleared.

With several results open, a forced close after a deferred one escapes this on `main` only because of #119, which keeps the registry from emptying. Once #119 is fixed, the two warnings appear with any number of results.

Holding off the deferred close while `clear_results()` clears fixes both, with the flag saved, unset and restored on exit:

```r
clear_results <- function(con) {
  disconnect <- meta(con, "disconnect")
  meta(con, "disconnect") <- FALSE
  on.exit(meta(con, "disconnect") <- disconnect)

  for (res in meta(con, "results")) {
```

With that, the forced close in the first example warns only about the open result and the query in the second only about the policy, while clearing `res2` still closes the connection. The test suite passes with it, on `main` as on the branch for #119.

title: Pin blockr.ci to a release instead of `@main`
description:
This repository calls blockr.ci at `@main`:

- Line 67 of [`.github/workflows/rcc.yaml`](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/a5073c8dfeff6739abdca45c05b458add0fc8752/.github/workflows/rcc.yaml#L67) calls `release-gate.yaml@main`

Each run uses whatever blockr.ci's `main` holds at that moment, so a change there reaches this repository's CI without a pull request here. The blockr.ci repository now publishes immutable releases, starting with [v0.1.0](https://github.com/BristolMyersSquibb/blockr.ci/releases/tag/v0.1.0), and a caller pinned to one runs blockr.ci's own actions from the tagged commit as well ([Versions](https://github.com/BristolMyersSquibb/blockr.ci/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#versions)).

Would it be worth pinning these to `v0.1.0`, or to its commit `1915d52313aaa13dd7e6ee1a5b3177f4c03f6986` with `# v0.1.0` as a comment, and adding a `.github/dependabot.yml` for the `github-actions` ecosystem so that upgrades arrive as pull requests? Changes to blockr.ci would then reach this repository only through those pull requests. Their CI runs with Dependabot secrets rather than Actions secrets, so any secret these calls pass needs adding there too. The workflow and job names stay the same, so required checks and rulesets need no change.

title: Clearing results in the order they were sent leaves one registered, breaking `dbDisconnect()`
description:
Clearing results in the order they were sent, as a function does that calls `on.exit(dbClearResult(res), add = TRUE)` for each, leaves the connection's result registry out of step: a later `dbClearResult()` removes the wrong entry or none, and `dbDisconnect()` then counts a result that was already cleared:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
res1 <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT 1")
res2 <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT 2")
dbClearResult(res1)
dbClearResult(res2)
dbDisconnect(con)
#> There are 1 result(s) in use. The connection will be released when they are closed
dbIsValid(con)
#> [1] TRUE
```

The id each result keeps is its position in the registry: `register_result()` sets it to the length of the list after appending the result ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/a5073c8dfeff6739abdca45c05b458add0fc8752/R/utils.R#L36-L37)), and `rm_result()` removes whatever sits at that position ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/a5073c8dfeff6739abdca45c05b458add0fc8752/R/utils.R#L53-L58)). Clearing `res1` moves `res2` from position 2 to 1, so clearing `res2` removes position 2, which no longer exists, and `res2` stays registered.

With three results, clearing the first two leaves the second, already cleared, in the registry and drops the third while it is still open. A forced `dbDisconnect(con, force = TRUE)` then clears the second result again, warning "Statement already released.", fails to release the connection and the database, which each report "has 1 unreleased child object", and still returns `TRUE`, while `dbIsValid(con)` stays `TRUE`.

Removing a result by identity rather than by position fixes both: with `rm_result()` dropping the entry whose metadata environment is the result's own, `dbDisconnect()` closes the connection in the first example, and the forced close in the second clears the third result and releases the connection without either message. The id is then no longer needed.

title: The `bigint` default documented for `dbConnect()` is not the one it uses
description:
The documentation of `dbConnect()` gives `bit64::integer64` as the `bigint` default if bit64 is installed, and `character` otherwise ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/dbConnect_AdbiDriver.R#L8-L10)). The default has been `"integer-strict"` since 641ec8b in December 2023 ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/AdbiConnection.R#L79-L93)), with bit64 installed as well:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
con@bigint
#> [1] "integer-strict"
```

The parameter documentation could name `"integer-strict"` as the default and list the values `resolve_bigint()` accepts: `"integer"`, `"integer-strict"`, `"numeric"`, `"numeric-strict"`, `"character"` and `"integer64"`. No help page lists them, and the strict modes are not mentioned anywhere.

title: Result leaks when a sent query fails to bind or execute, breaking `dbDisconnect()`
description:
A query sent with `params` whose binding fails, or with `immediate = TRUE` whose execution fails, leaves its result registered with the connection, so `dbDisconnect()` no longer closes it:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
try(dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT ?", params = list(1L, 2L)))
#> Error : Expecting equally many `params` components as placeholders.
try(dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM missing", immediate = TRUE))
#> Error in adbcdrivermanager::adbc_statement_execute_query(x@statement,  :
#>   INVALID_ARGUMENT: [SQLite] Failed to prepare query: no such table: missing
#> query: SELECT * FROM missing
dbDisconnect(con)
#> There are 2 result(s) in use. The connection will be released when they are closed
dbIsValid(con)
#> [1] TRUE
```

The Arrow versions, `dbGetQueryArrow()` and `dbSendQueryArrow()`, leave their results behind the same way.

Both `dbSendQuery()` and `dbSendQueryArrow()` create the result, which `init_result()` registers with the connection ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/dfab0424fb4c6019b90cb3514d5e516b8f315fe2/R/AdbiResult.R#L90)), before binding `params` or executing it ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/dfab0424fb4c6019b90cb3514d5e516b8f315fe2/R/dbSendQuery_AdbiConnection_character.R#L71-L88), [source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/dfab0424fb4c6019b90cb3514d5e516b8f315fe2/R/dbSendQueryArrow_AdbiConnection.R#L16-L33)). An error in either step leaves the method without returning the result, so the caller has nothing to clear, and `dbDisconnect()` then only marks the connection for release once its results are closed ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/dfab0424fb4c6019b90cb3514d5e516b8f315fe2/R/dbDisconnect_AdbiConnection.R#L26-L36)).

For statements, #114 clears the result when binding or execution fails in `dbSendStatement()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/dfab0424fb4c6019b90cb3514d5e516b8f315fe2/R/dbSendStatement_AdbiConnection_character.R#L25-L36)). With the same guard in both query methods, both calls above fail without leaving a result behind, and `dbDisconnect()` returns `TRUE`.

This is separate from #73, where the statement leaks before any result exists, when `init_result()` fails to prepare it.

title: Statements from `dbSendStatement()` only run when `dbGetRowsAffected()` is called
description:
Unless it is sent with `immediate = TRUE`, a statement from `dbSendStatement()` runs only once `dbGetRowsAffected()` asks for its count, so one that is cleared without that call never runs:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbWriteTable(con, "t", data.frame(a = 1:10))
res <- dbSendStatement(con, "DELETE FROM t WHERE a > 8")
dbClearResult(res)
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM t")
#>    n
#> 1 10
```

The same holds for a statement bound with `dbBind()`. DBI documents `dbSendStatement()` as executing the statement ([DBI](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/blob/bd59d19c9fa5bcbf8972dd4af78240ab6d8e4cd2/R/dbSendStatement.R#L3-L5)), with `dbGetRowsAffected()` an optional step ([DBI](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/blob/bd59d19c9fa5bcbf8972dd4af78240ab6d8e4cd2/R/15-dbBind.R#L117-L124)).

The method executes on send only if the caller passed `immediate = TRUE` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/dbSendStatement_AdbiConnection_character.R#L29-L31)). With the default `NULL`, `init_result()` does work out from the parameter schema that the statement takes no parameters ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/AdbiResult.R#L61-L73)), but the method does not use that, and execution waits for `dbGetRowsAffected()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/dbGetRowsAffected_AdbiResult.R#L17-L19)).

Executing in `dbSendStatement()` when the resolved `immediate` is `TRUE`, and in `dbBind()` for a statement, makes both cases run on the branch of #106. The test suite, DBItest included, then passes except for four expectations that `dbHasCompleted()` is `FALSE` right after a statement is bound ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/tests/testthat/test-parameters.R#L124-L128)), where DBItest specifies that it always returns `TRUE` for a `dbSendStatement()` result ([DBItest](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBItest/blob/42d9c05f4668faa50e4d7a331c5c8f7d97d34064/R/spec-meta-has-completed.R#L24-L30)).

title: On SQLite, statements report `-1` rows affected, which the test helper turns into skips
description:
With adbcsqlite, every statement reports `-1` rows affected:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbWriteTable(con, "t", data.frame(a = 1:10))
dbExecute(con, "DELETE FROM t WHERE a < 6")
#> [1] -1
```

Through adbcpostgresql, the same statement returns 5.

The cause is in adbi, whose `execute_statement()` passes a result stream to `adbc_statement_execute_query()` for `dbSendStatement()` results too ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/8106f7ca76a116a3496f51cb80ddb1b69a932602/R/dbFetch_AdbiResult.R#L130-L150)). ADBC's driver framework executes a statement given a stream as a query, and one without as an update ([source](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/framework/statement.h#L140-L144)). The SQLite driver's query path returns `-1` ([source](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/sqlite/sqlite.cc#L1066-L1084)), while its update path counts `sqlite3_changes()` ([source](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/sqlite/sqlite.cc#L1128-L1130)).

The DBItest helper hides this. Its `rows_affected_callback` turns `-1` into `skip()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/8106f7ca76a116a3496f51cb80ddb1b69a932602/tests/testthat/helper-DBItest.R#L9-L17)), and because `dbCreateTable()`, `dbRemoveTable()` and `dbAppendTable()` all go through `dbExecute()`, the skip also ends tests that are not about row counts. On `main` it skips 164 of the 659 tests. With the callback replaced by `identity`, 3358 more expectations pass and 42 tests fail:

| Tests | Failure |
|---|---|
| 11 | The row count is `-1` |
| 20 | Values are equal but not identical; `create_table_name`, for one, reads an empty `DOUBLE` column back as integer |
| 6 | #72, including four transaction tests |
| 5 | Appending raw, 64-bit, invalid and factor values |

With the `temporary_tables = FALSE` tweak removed as well (#83), `remove_table_temporary_arg` also fails, which is #91. These numbers come from DBItest 1.8.3, adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2, adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-3 and arrow 25.0.1, the versions CI installs.

Running `dbSendStatement()` results without a stream fixes the count. With that change to `execute_statement()` on `main`, the `DELETE` above returns 5, the 11 row-count failures pass, no other test changes, and the callback never fires. The other 31 failures then surface, so the same change has to drop the callback and either fix those failures or skip them with a reason each. I can open a PR.

One caveat is upstream. Without a stream, adbcsqlite reports the previous statement's count for DDL, because its update path adds `sqlite3_changes()` for any statement without result columns, and SQLite leaves that value unchanged after DDL ([docs](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/changes.html)). A `CREATE TABLE` run right after an `UPDATE` of 3 rows reports 3.

title: DBItest's `begin_write_disconnect` no longer segfaults on Linux
description:
The skip list has skipped `begin_write_disconnect` since fea85fd in August 2023, listed as causing segfaults ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/tests/testthat/test-DBItest.R#L52-L53)). On Linux, with R 4.6.1, adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2 and adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-3, both of its stages pass, on their own and in a full DBItest run with `package_name` as the only skip.

Dropping the entry would let CI show whether it still crashes on macOS or Windows, which I have not checked.

title: Run the DBItest tests that need an adbi option with that option set
description:
Six tests on the DBItest skip list only need an adbi option set ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/tests/testthat/test-DBItest.R#L12-L20)). The tests `send_query_only_one_result_set`, `send_statement_only_one_result_set` and `arrow_send_query_only_one_result_set` need `options(adbi.allow_multiple_results = FALSE)`, and `send_query_stale_warning`, `send_statement_stale_warning` and `arrow_send_query_stale_warning` need `options(adbi.force_close_results = TRUE)`. Run through `DBItest::test_some()` inside `withr::with_options()` with the option they need, all six pass on the branch of #106.

A `test_that()` block per option that runs them that way would take them off the skip list and cover what the two options switch on, which no other test does.

title: Creating a table from a list of raw vectors fails with a `NULL` entry or on PostgreSQL
description:
A column that is a list of raw vectors gets its type in `dbDataType()` from DBI's ANSI mapping rather than from the mapping adbi has for blob objects, and `dbCreateTable()` fails on it in two cases. A `NULL` entry, which is how such a list holds a missing value, makes the ANSI mapping fail with any driver:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbCreateTable(con, "t", data.frame(a = I(list(as.raw(1:2), NULL))))
#> Error: Only lists of raw vectors are currently supported
```

Without one, the ANSI mapping gives `BLOB`, a type PostgreSQL does not have, so the `CREATE TABLE` fails there (adbcpostgresql 0.24.0-1, PostgreSQL 17.11).

The blob mapping is used only for objects of class `blob` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/dbDataType_AdbiConnection.R#L12-L18)), and the list method of the ANSI mapping rejects every element that is not a raw vector ([DBI](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/blob/bd59d19c9fa5bcbf8972dd4af78240ab6d8e4cd2/R/dbiDataType_list.R#L1-L7)), although DBI's own `dbQuoteLiteral()` writes a `NULL` entry of such a list as SQL `NULL`.

Sending a list whose elements are all raw vectors or `NULL` through the blob mapping too fixes both cases: on a copy of `main`, `dbCreateTable()` then creates the column as `BLOB` on SQLite and as `bytea` on PostgreSQL. The blob mapping has no entry for DuckDB ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/utils.R#L87-L98)), where blob objects already fail in `dbDataType()` with DuckDB 1.5.5, so it needs `duckdb = "BLOB"` as well for such a list to keep the `BLOB` it gets there now. With both changes, both kinds of column work with all three drivers, the test suite passes, and so does DBItest's `append_roundtrip_raw`, which the skip list in #106 skips for the `NULL` entry.

Related to #15.

title: Appending with `dbWriteTable()` fails when the table does not exist
description:
With `append = TRUE`, `dbWriteTable()` fails when the table does not exist yet, where DBI specifies that it is created ([DBItest](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBItest/blob/42d9c05f4668faa50e4d7a331c5c8f7d97d34064/R/spec-sql-write-table.R#L233-L239)):

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbWriteTable(con, "t", data.frame(a = 1:2), append = TRUE)
#> Error: INTERNAL: failed to prepare: no such table: main.t
#> query was: INSERT INTO main . "t" ("a") VALUES (?)
```

It fails with adbcpostgresql 0.24.0-1 against PostgreSQL 17.11, and with DuckDB 1.5.5, as well.

The method passes `append = TRUE` on as ADBC's `append` ingest mode ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/85d67c87cf68ee46c27e41b06841418fb1c24ea6/R/dbWriteTable_AdbiConnection_Id_data.frame.R#L110-L125)), which needs an existing table. The `create_append` mode creates the table when it does not exist and appends to it otherwise ([adbc.h](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/include/arrow-adbc/adbc.h#L819-L823)).

With `create_append` in its place, on a copy of `main`, the call above creates the table and a second call appends to it, with all three drivers. DBItest's `append_table_new` then passes and the rest of the suite still does, which would take `append_table_new` off the skip list, where it is listed under "poorly understood causes". The mode works back to adbcsqlite 0.11.0.1, the floor in Suggests, where appending with incompatible columns still fails as it should.

title: Printing a connection fails when its driver does not implement `GetInfo`
description:
Printing a connection whose driver does not implement `GetInfo` fails after the header line. The monkey driver that `adbi()` uses by default is one:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi())
con
#> <AdbiConnection>
#> Error in adbcdrivermanager::adbc_connection_get_info(object@connection,  :
#>   NOT_IMPLEMENTED: GetInfo
```

The `show()` method calls `adbc_connection_get_info()` without a handler ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/3accd5b21c4d70e265a17601678708b539085f3a/R/show_AdbiConnection.R#L17-L22)). The monkey driver's connection is adbcdrivermanager's void connection, which does not override `GetInfoImpl()` and so inherits the ADBC driver framework's default, `NotImplemented("GetInfo")` ([driver](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/r/adbcdrivermanager/src/driver_test.cc#L155), [framework](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/framework/base_driver.h#L869-L871)). Any other driver built on that framework that leaves `GetInfoImpl()` alone behaves the same.

Would it make sense to catch `adbc_status_not_implemented` around that call, as `db_vendor_name()` already does for the same lookup ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/3accd5b21c4d70e265a17601678708b539085f3a/R/utils.R#L123-L126)), and print only the header in that case? With that handler and the info lines skipped, the monkey connection prints `<AdbiConnection>` alone, and a SQLite connection prints exactly as before.

Measured with adbi at 3accd5b and adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-1. I can open a PR.

title: Statement leaks when a query fails to prepare, breaking `dbDisconnect()`
description:
When `init_result()` fails after creating the ADBC statement, the statement is never released. The statement is created on the first line below, and an error from `adbc_statement_set_sql_query()` or `adbc_statement_prepare()` leaves it unreachable:

https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/55e7ba567bd5777d49d916b4f444fa66e16c88b5/R/AdbiResult.R#L54-L62

Until the garbage collector releases it, the connection has an unreleased child, so a following `dbDisconnect()` releases neither the connection nor the database, yet returns `TRUE`; the connection stays valid. A syntax error is enough:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi("adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
try(dbGetQuery(con, "SELEC 1"))
#> Error in adbcdrivermanager::adbc_statement_prepare(stmt) :
#>   INVALID_ARGUMENT: [SQLite] Failed to prepare query: near "SELEC": syntax error
#> query: SELEC 1
con@connection$.child_count
#> [1] 1
dbDisconnect(con)
#> <adbcsqlite_connection/adbc_connection/adbc_xptr> has 1 unreleased child object
#> <adbcsqlite_database/adbc_database/adbc_xptr> has 1 unreleased child object
dbIsValid(con)
#> [1] TRUE
```

The disconnect still returns `TRUE` because `adbc_release()` turns the release errors into messages:

https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/55e7ba567bd5777d49d916b4f444fa66e16c88b5/R/utils.R#L93-L96

Releasing `stmt` on exit in `init_result()`, and clearing the handler once the result object owns it, as #59 does for the connection, would fix the leak.

title: Printing a connection shows `NA: NA` for the driver's ADBC version
description:
Printing a connection ends in an `NA: NA` line, with both adbcsqlite and adbcpostgresql:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
con
#> <AdbiConnection>
#>   Vendor name: SQLite
#>   Vendor version: 3.45.1
#>   Driver name: ADBC SQLite Driver
#>   Driver version: (unknown)
#>   Driver arrow version: 0.9.0-SNAPSHOT
#>   NA: NA
```

The `show()` method fetches every code the driver reports, but labels only six of them and reads only their `string_value` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/07beee3a20cf8c6a78ce2cee2af3832978627b84/R/show_AdbiConnection.R#L8-L24)). Both drivers also report code 103, the driver's ADBC API version, which is an `int64` ([header](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/include/arrow-adbc/adbc.h#L520-L528), [SQLite](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/sqlite/sqlite.cc#L671-L675), [PostgreSQL](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/driver/postgresql/connection.cc#L59-L63)), so its label and its value both print as `NA`.

Requesting only the six labelled codes would fix this, since a driver leaves out any requested code it does not recognize ([header](https://github.com/apache/arrow-adbc/blob/769e340d9193846366357d969da93d787e928383/c/include/arrow-adbc/adbc.h#L1539-L1542)). With `nms` defined before the call and `as.integer(names(nms))` passed to `adbc_connection_get_info()`, the last line is gone with both drivers and the other five are unchanged. It would also keep out any further code a driver may report, which the method would currently print with an `NA` label as well.

Measured with adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2, adbcpostgresql 0.24.0-1 and adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-1. I can open a PR.

title: The `dbAppendTable()` method accepts a list and converts factors without a warning
description:
The `dbAppendTable()` method misses two requirements of the [DBI specification](https://dbi.r-dbi.org/reference/dbAppendTable.html): when the new data "is not a data frame or has different column names, an error is raised; the remote table remains unchanged", and a factor is "returned as character, with a warning". Neither happens:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbCreateTable(con, "t", data.frame(a = 1.5))
dbAppendTable(con, "t", list(a = 2.5))
#> [1] -1
dbReadTable(con, "t")
#>     a
#> 1 2.5
dbCreateTable(con, "f", data.frame(a = "x"))
dbAppendTable(con, "f", data.frame(a = factor("y")))
#> [1] -1
```

The `-1` is #92. On the same calls, RSQLite fails with `is.data.frame(value) is not TRUE` and warns "Factors converted to character".

Both checks live in code that adbi's method replaces. DBI's default `dbAppendTable()` starts with `stopifnot(is.data.frame(value))` and inserts through bound parameters ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/blob/2481a2204602232c3804d3e8f8520170164c4294/R/dbAppendTable_DBIConnection.R#L13-L24)), and RSQLite warns while binding ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/blob/201287ef6db6dce4d5c3e13b1ae6453ea0f570f3/R/db_bind.R#L47), [`factor_to_string()`](https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/blob/201287ef6db6dce4d5c3e13b1ae6453ea0f570f3/R/coerce.R#L11-L18)). The adbi method instead passes `value` straight to `sqlAppendTable()` and runs the resulting `INSERT` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/590c4a4534ad92d676049f6cfa5d1a03044519d8/R/dbAppendTable_AdbiConnection_character_data.frame.R#L3-L23)), and the `sqlData()` step there converts factors to character without a warning.

DBItest's `append_table_invalid_value` and `append_roundtrip_factor` cover both, but the `rows_affected` callback skips them before they reach the checks (#92).

Would it work to add both checks at the top of the adbi method, the data-frame check as in DBI and a warning on factor columns as in RSQLite? They do not depend on how the rows are inserted, so they would carry over if #17 moves the method to ADBC ingest. I can open a PR.

title: Metadata lookups leak their ADBC streams, breaking `dbDisconnect()`
description:
Each call that reads connection metadata leaves an ADBC stream unreleased until the garbage collector finalizes it. Measured one call at a time, `dbExistsTable()`, `dbListTables()` and `show()` leave one stream each, and `dbListFields()` and `dbGetInfo()` leave two. As with the statement in #73, the connection then has unreleased children, so a following `dbDisconnect()` releases neither the connection nor the database, yet returns `TRUE`, and the connection keeps answering queries:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbExistsTable(con, "x")
#> [1] FALSE
con@connection$.child_count
#> [1] 1
dbDisconnect(con)
#> <adbcsqlite_connection/adbc_connection/adbc_xptr> has 1 unreleased child object
#> <adbcsqlite_database/adbc_database/adbc_xptr> has 1 unreleased child object
dbIsValid(con)
#> [1] TRUE
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 1 AS a")
#>   a
#> 1 1
```

An explicit `gc()` brings the count back to 0, so whether a disconnect fails depends on whether a collection ran since the last such call.

All four places that read metadata pass the stream from `adbc_connection_get_objects()` or `adbc_connection_get_info()` to `nanoarrow::convert_array_stream()`, which reads it to the end without releasing it, and none of them releases it afterwards:

- The internal `get_schema_objects()`, behind `dbExistsTable()`, `dbListTables()` and `dbListFields()` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/aae2d3c6a63ec40fbab12553526eaaa0d82cb90a/R/dbListTables_AdbiConnection.R#L100-L111))
- The `dbGetInfo()` method itself ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/aae2d3c6a63ec40fbab12553526eaaa0d82cb90a/R/dbGetInfo_AdbiConnection.R#L9-L11))
- The helper `connection_info_string()`, called by `dbGetInfo()` and by `db_vendor_name()`, so `dbDataType()` on a blob leaks as well with a driver loaded through the Driver Manager ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/aae2d3c6a63ec40fbab12553526eaaa0d82cb90a/R/utils.R#L108-L114))
- The `show()` method ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/aae2d3c6a63ec40fbab12553526eaaa0d82cb90a/R/show_AdbiConnection.R#L8-L10))

Releasing each stream once it is converted would fix this. With this helper used at all four sites in place of `nanoarrow::convert_array_stream()`, none of these calls leaves a child behind, the `dbDisconnect()` above invalidates the connection, and no test in the suite changes its result:

```r
convert_stream <- function(stream) {
  on.exit(stream$release())
  nanoarrow::convert_array_stream(stream)
}
```

Measured with adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2, adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-1 and nanoarrow 0.9.0. I can open a PR.

title: Removing a temporary table with `dbRemoveTable()` fails on SQLite and PostgreSQL
description:
With `temporary = TRUE`, `dbRemoveTable()` sends `DROP TEMPORARY TABLE` ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/8106f7ca76a116a3496f51cb80ddb1b69a932602/R/dbRemoveTable_AdbiConnection_character.R#L15-L23)). The `TEMPORARY` keyword is [MySQL syntax](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/drop-table.html), and neither SQLite nor PostgreSQL accepts it:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi(pkg = "adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbWriteTable(con, "x", data.frame(a = 1), temporary = TRUE)
dbRemoveTable(con, "x", temporary = TRUE)
#> Error in adbcdrivermanager::adbc_statement_prepare(stmt) :
#>   INVALID_ARGUMENT: [SQLite] Failed to prepare query: near "TEMPORARY": syntax error
#> query: DROP TEMPORARY TABLE "x"
```

Through adbcpostgresql against PostgreSQL 17, the same call fails with `syntax error at or near "TEMPORARY"`. The keyword has been there since the initial commit, so every release carries it. It also breaks `dbWriteTable(temporary = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)`, whose overwrite branch calls `dbRemoveTable(temporary = TRUE)` first ([source](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/8106f7ca76a116a3496f51cb80ddb1b69a932602/R/dbWriteTable_AdbiConnection_Id_data.frame.R#L109-L110)). That call fails before anything is dropped, so unlike #72 it loses no data.

No test catches it. None of adbi's own tests pass `temporary`, and DBItest's `remove_table_temporary_arg` is switched off by the `temporary_tables = FALSE` tweak (#83). With the tweak removed, the `rows_affected_callback` in `helper-DBItest.R` still skips the test one line before the call, and with the callback out of the way as well, the test fails at the call.

RSQLite and RPostgres qualify the name with the temporary schema instead ([RSQLite](https://github.com/r-dbi/RSQLite/blob/201287ef6db6dce4d5c3e13b1ae6453ea0f570f3/R/dbRemoveTable_SQLiteConnection_character.R#L14-L18), [RPostgres](https://github.com/r-dbi/RPostgres/blob/1a889b70f7fd801977c62932c145234fb0bed851/R/dbRemoveTable_PqConnection_character.R#L18-L25)). Sent through adbi, `DROP TABLE temp."x"` on SQLite and `DROP TABLE pg_temp."x"` on PostgreSQL remove only the temporary table, leave a permanent table of the same name untouched, and fail when called again, which is what the DBItest test asserts. Deleting the keyword alone would be worse than the current error, because an unqualified `DROP TABLE "x"` removes the permanent table when no temporary one exists.

ADBC has no call for dropping a table, so adbi has to supply the qualifier. The vendor name that `adbc_connection_get_info()` reports (`"SQLite"`, `"PostgreSQL"`) could select it, with a clear error for other databases, since DBI allows a backend not to support `temporary`. Until then, `dbRemoveTable(con, Id(schema = "temp", table = "x"))` works, or `schema = "pg_temp"` on PostgreSQL.

The overwrite path can avoid the SQL altogether. Its TODO waits on ADBC's `replace` ingest mode, and apache/arrow-adbc#1355 was closed in March 2024. With adbcsqlite 0.24.0.2 and adbcpostgresql 0.24.0.1, `replace` combined with `adbc.ingest.temporary` replaces only the temporary table, so switching to it would fix this path and #72 together. I can open a PR.

title: Binding a POSIXlt value with `dbBind()` fails with an unsupported struct type
description:
A POSIXlt parameter reaches the driver as a struct column, so the query fails when it runs:

``` r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi("adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")

res <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT ? AS x", immediate = FALSE)
dbBind(res, list(as.POSIXlt("2020-01-01 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")))
dbFetch(res)
#> Error: NOT_IMPLEMENTED: Column 0 has unsupported type struct
```

The DBI spec lists POSIXlt timestamps among the types `dbBind()` accepts ([`man/dbBind.Rd#L232-L244`](https://github.com/r-dbi/DBI/blob/2481a2204602232c3804d3e8f8520170164c4294/man/dbBind.Rd#L232-L244)). The `I()` wrapping in `dbBind()` ([`R/dbBind_AdbiResult.R#L28-L31`](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/a6213b3c03448a1a59098741ae5e3362f40cfa16/R/dbBind_AdbiResult.R#L28-L31)) keeps the value a POSIXlt when the parameters become a data frame, where `data.frame()` alone would turn it into POSIXct. From there, nanoarrow represents POSIXlt as a struct of its components by design ([`r/R/schema.R#L114-L117`](https://github.com/apache/arrow-nanoarrow/blob/8f81815c7a233d3fc697f43c7aed42e82a4f33be/r/R/schema.R#L114-L117)). The error is the same with and without arrow installed.

DBItest does not catch this, because its `bind_timestamp_lt` test skips unless the `timestamp_typed` tweak is set, and the SQLite context sets it to `FALSE` ([`tests/testthat/helper-DBItest.R#L31`](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/a6213b3c03448a1a59098741ae5e3362f40cfa16/tests/testthat/helper-DBItest.R#L31)).

Converting POSIXlt to POSIXct next to the existing factor conversion fixes it:

``` r
lt <- vapply(params, inherits, logical(1L), "POSIXlt")
params[lt] <- lapply(params[lt], as.POSIXct)
```

With these two lines in `dbBind_AdbiResult()`, the example returns `2020-01-01T12:00:00.000000`, and a POSIXlt in Europe/Zurich, `NA` included, binds exactly like the equivalent POSIXct.

title: Overwriting a table with `dbWriteTable()` drops it and then fails
description:
Calling `dbWriteTable()` with `overwrite = TRUE` removes the existing table, then fails before writing the new one, so the table is lost:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(adbi::adbi("adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
dbWriteTable(con, "x", data.frame(a = 1))
dbWriteTable(con, "x", data.frame(a = 2), overwrite = TRUE)
#> Error in paste0("adbc.ingest.mode.", mode) :
#>   cannot coerce type 'closure' to vector of type 'character'
dbExistsTable(con, "x")
#> [1] FALSE
```

The same error occurs when the table does not exist yet, where `overwrite = TRUE` should simply create it.

The `overwrite` branch of `dbWriteTable_AdbiConnection_Id_data.frame()` drops the table without assigning `mode` ([lines 105–113](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/f23662b2f09dbb8ee342e81870af1859e12421b8/R/dbWriteTable_AdbiConnection_Id_data.frame.R#L105-L113)), so the `paste0()` that builds the ingest mode ([line 120](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/f23662b2f09dbb8ee342e81870af1859e12421b8/R/dbWriteTable_AdbiConnection_Id_data.frame.R#L120)) finds `base::mode()` instead. The branch has looked like this since 7193a78, which replaced ADBC's `replace` ingest mode with dropping the table first. Every release since then contains it (v0.1.0, v0.1.1 and v0.1.2).

DBItest's `overwrite_table` and `overwrite_table_missing` would catch this, but both are reported as skipped. The `DROP TABLE` that `dbRemoveTable()` sends through `dbExecute()` has an unknown affected-row count, and the `rows_affected_callback` in `helper-DBItest.R` ([lines 9–17](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/f23662b2f09dbb8ee342e81870af1859e12421b8/tests/testthat/helper-DBItest.R#L9-L17)) turns that into `skip()`. The skip fires inside the overwrite call, after the drop and before the failing `paste0()`.

Assigning `mode <- "create"` after `dbRemoveTable()` should fix it, with a test that overwrites a table and reads it back without going through that callback. I can open a PR.

title: Raise `dbitest_version` in the DBItest helper to 1.8.3
description:
The DBItest context in `tests/testthat/helper-DBItest.R` sets `dbitest_version = "1.8.0"` under a `# FIXME: Bump` comment, so DBItest skips every test added after 1.8.0. On `main` that is 47 of the 659 tests, 45 of them Arrow tests, including the four `arrow_*_temporary_*` tests. The `DESCRIPTION` already requires DBItest 1.8.3.

Setting it to `"1.8.3"` turns 40 of them on. With DBItest 1.8.3, adbcsqlite 0.24.0-2, adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0-3 and arrow 25.0.1, as CI installs them, 7 pass, 28 run until the `rows_affected_callback` skips them (#92), and 5 fail. All five are Arrow versions of SQL tests:

- The tests `arrow_read_table_arrow_empty` and `arrow_create_table_arrow_visible_in_other_connection` fail the same way as `read_table_empty` and `create_table_visible_in_other_connection`, which the skip list already excludes for apache/arrow-adbc#1400 and apache/arrow-adbc#1591. An empty table reads back with the wrong column types.
- In `arrow_write_table_arrow_visible_in_other_connection`, the callback skips the first stage after DBI's default `dbWriteTableArrow()` has created the table but before it inserts any rows, so the later stages read an empty table. With the callback replaced by `identity`, all three stages pass.

The fix is to set `dbitest_version = "1.8.3"`, drop the FIXME, and add those three tests to the skip list.

title: Re-enable DBItest's temporary-table tests
description:
The DBItest context in `tests/testthat/helper-DBItest.R` sets `temporary_tables = FALSE`, citing apache/arrow-adbc#1141. That issue was closed on 2024-03-25, and the setting no longer seems needed: without it, DBItest's temporary-table tests raise no failures against adbcsqlite.

Measured on `main` (fb2184b) with DBItest 1.8.3.9010, adbcsqlite 0.24.0.2 and adbcdrivermanager 0.24.0.1, over the 14 DBItest tests whose names contain `temporary`:

| Tests | With `temporary_tables = FALSE` | Without it |
|---|---|---|
| `create_table_temporary_2`, `temporary_table_2` | skipped by the setting | pass |
| `temporary_table_1`, `remove_table_temporary`, `remove_table_temporary_arg` | skipped by the setting | pass until a `rows_affected` check, then skip |
| `list_tables_temporary`, `exists_table_temporary`, `list_objects_temporary`, `list_fields_temporary` | pass, with their temporary-table checks switched off | pass until a `rows_affected` check, then skip |
| `create_table_temporary_1` | skipped by the setting | skips at a `rows_affected` check |
| The four `arrow_*_temporary_*` tests | skipped by `dbitest_version` | skipped by `dbitest_version` |

The `rows_affected` skips come from the helper's `rows_affected_callback`, which skips whenever adbcsqlite reports `-1` rows affected. They are not specific to temporary tables.

Across the whole suite, run with `testthat::test_local()`, dropping the setting takes the passing expectations from 2542 to 2564, with no failures or errors either way. The arrow package was not installed for either run, so the Arrow tests were skipped in both.

title: Binding plain R values with `dbBind()` fails without the arrow package
description:
Without the arrow package installed, binding a double, integer, character or logical value fails:

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(adbi::adbi("adbcsqlite"), uri = ":memory:")
res <- DBI::dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT ? AS x", immediate = FALSE)
DBI::dbBind(res, list(1.5))
#> Error: Package 'arrow' required for create double array from object of type AsIs
```

The README's own example (`dbBind(res, 30)`) fails the same way. Date, POSIXct and blob values bind fine.

The cause is in `dbBind_AdbiResult()`, which wraps every parameter in `I()` before building the data frame ([`R/dbBind_AdbiResult.R#L29`](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/312771fecf03a418310280c9b852a1e98ad3723a/R/dbBind_AdbiResult.R#L29)). For an `AsIs` vector of a base type, nanoarrow falls back to arrow, which adbi only suggests.

The `I()` wrapping dates from 5f36103; the nanoarrow methods for `AsIs` that adbi registered at the time (fd4a193) were removed in b71d042.

The test suite does not catch this because the DBItest runner skips all `bind_*` tests when arrow is missing ([`tests/testthat/test-DBItest.R#L57`](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/312771fecf03a418310280c9b852a1e98ad3723a/tests/testthat/test-DBItest.R#L57)).

Dropping the `AsIs` class again right after `as.data.frame()` fixes it. With this line added, all seven types above bind with arrow unavailable:

```r
params[] <- lapply(params, function(x) structure(x, class = setdiff(class(x), "AsIs")))
```

title: Lint checks names against the installed adbi, without testthat attached
description:
The `object_usage_linter` run by `lintr::lint_package()` looks names up in `getNamespace("adbi")`, which loads the installed copy, and beyond that in the lint session's search path, which doesn't include testthat ([`make_check_env()`](https://github.com/r-lib/lintr/blob/ae8cda850cbbd07191ed7fbd12d7e967353ebe45/R/object_usage_linter.R#L169-L176)). That gives two kinds of false positive:

- Calls into adbi are checked against whatever copy is installed. Without one, `object_usage_linter` reports 210 false positives on main, for calls to adbi's internal functions and imports. With an older copy, internal functions added since are flagged: linting #69 merged into main, with main's adbi installed, flags `get_parameter_schema()`.
- A testthat function called inside a helper function in `tests/testthat` is flagged as "no visible global function definition", although testthat is attached when the tests run. On #69 merged into main, that hits `skip_if_not_installed()` and `local_mocked_bindings()` in `local_parameter_connection()`, which would fail the required `rcc` check.

CI avoids the first by installing the package before it lints ([`rcc.yaml`](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/3ae135b758ca56d1996cdd35ad20c69f831f9611/.github/workflows/rcc.yaml#L38-L45)); a local run depends on what happens to be installed. Nothing avoids the second.

Loading the checkout at the top of `.lintr.R` fixes both, since `pkgload::load_all()` registers the checkout's namespace and, for a package that uses testthat, attaches it:

```r
# Resolve names against this checkout rather than an installed copy, and
# attach testthat as the test run does. Since lintr evaluates this file with
# sys.source(), its path is in that call's `file` argument.
pkgload::load_all(dirname(dynGet("file")), helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
```

With adbi uninstalled and this line added, main lints clean whether `lintr::lint_package()` runs from the package root, from outside it, or from inside another package, and the two testthat lints on #69 are gone. The path comes from the `file` argument of the `sys.source()` call that evaluates `.lintr.R` ([`settings.R`](https://github.com/r-lib/lintr/blob/ae8cda850cbbd07191ed7fbd12d7e967353ebe45/R/settings.R#L106)). A plain `pkgload::load_all()` would resolve `.` against the working directory instead: from outside a package it errors, and from inside another package it loads that package, and the false positives come back.

The line adds about a second to a lint run. With `helpers = FALSE` it doesn't source `helper-DBItest.R`. The pkgload package comes with roxygen2, which the lint job installs, and `.lintr.R` is build-ignored, so `R CMD check` is unaffected.

title: Add a reverse dependency check with `r-devel/recheck`
description:
Since #71 replaced the CI, nothing checks adbi's reverse dependencies. The revdep workflows it removed had never run (#70), and the 0.1.3 release did the check by hand (#76), running each CRAN dependent against the new tarball with `tools::check_packages_in_dir()`. The release gate's comment on #77 meanwhile points readers at a `recheck` job in the pull request's checks, which this repository does not have.

## Plan

Add a workflow, `recheck` (`.github/workflows/recheck.yaml`), that calls the reusable workflow from [r-devel/recheck](https://github.com/r-devel/recheck). It checks every dependent twice, against the CRAN release of adbi and against the branch, and reports what changed between the two.

- **Dependents:** `which: most`. The three on CRAN, db2pq, dbplyr and fabricQueryR, list adbi in `Suggests` only, so the default, `strong`, would check none of them.
- **Triggers:** by hand through `workflow_dispatch`, on any branch, and on pull requests carrying the `release` label, next to the release gate.
- **Not required:** upstream calls a reverse dependency check "typically too volatile to use as an automatic pass/fail CI test", so the result is for reading rather than gating.

## When it can first run

The old version comes from CRAN ([`recheck.yml#L80-L85`](https://github.com/r-devel/recheck/blob/ef259e57a8712b89bfb3093a73e082f5fdde79fe/.github/workflows/recheck.yml#L80-L85)), and CRAN has had no adbi since the archival (#61). Until 0.1.3 is accepted, a run therefore fails. The `oldpkg` leg has nothing to check, and its last call, `tools::summarize_check_packages_in_dir_results()`, errors on the empty directory with "attempt to set 'rownames' on an object with no dimensions" (replayed with R 4.6.1). The check matrix keeps GitHub's default `fail-fast` ([L111-L113](https://github.com/r-devel/recheck/blob/ef259e57a8712b89bfb3093a73e082f5fdde79fe/.github/workflows/recheck.yml#L111-L113)), so that failure cancels the `newpkg` leg as well.

None of this stops the workflow from merging now. A `workflow_dispatch` trigger only works once the file is on the default branch, so merging has to come first anyway, and the first run worth reading is the one after CRAN accepts 0.1.3.

title: Deprecate R package names passed as `driver` to `adbi()`
description:
With #60, a string passed as `driver` to `adbi()` names an ADBC Driver Manager driver or manifest, and R package drivers are selected with the new `pkg` argument. For compatibility, a string that names an installed R package with a same-named driver function still selects that package's driver, so `adbi("adbcsqlite")` keeps working without a warning. This issue tracks retiring that fallback, so that what a `driver` string means no longer depends on which R packages happen to be installed.

## Plan

1. The next release, the first with `pkg`: no warning yet. Notify the maintainers below.
2. The release after that: warn via `.Deprecated()`, pointing to `adbi(pkg = "<name>")`.
3. A later release: drop the fallback, so that `driver` strings only reach the Driver Manager.

Passing the driver object, as in `adbi(adbcsqlite::adbcsqlite())`, works on every adbi version without a warning, so callers can switch before the release with `pkg` reaches CRAN. The `pkg` spelling needs that release as a minimum version.

## Notify downstream

Each of these calls `adbi()` with an R package name:

- [ ] Notify dbplyr: [a test](https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/blob/f478e2070c9a60f4aebcc94132048312209dd097/tests/testthat/test-backend-adbc.R#L22) and [a commented-out example](https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/blob/f478e2070c9a60f4aebcc94132048312209dd097/R/backend-adbc.R#L37)
- [ ] Notify db2pq: [package code](https://github.com/iangow/db2pqr/blob/f2591ebabf031e17c8a90c27197c3c97263b2191/R/tbl_to_pq_dev.R#L497)
- [ ] Notify mirai: [three calls in a vignette](https://github.com/r-lib/mirai/blob/4986ee4a5dc8998e888331c156f1b61a30127491/vignettes/v03-serialization.Rmd#L255)
- [ ] Notify kangaroo (not on CRAN): [package code](https://github.com/iangow/kangaroo/blob/71f03317839aed8f46f8907918b641cfe7ea2487/R/driver.R#L6)
- [ ] Notify OmopOnPostgres (not on CRAN): [package code](https://github.com/OHDSI/OmopOnPostgres/blob/8d41258acc67a7d0dc48fcbd3af72a1b32540b18/R/postgresSource.R#L47)
- [ ] Notify duckhttp (not on CRAN): [a `data-raw` script](https://github.com/KTH-Library/duckhttp/blob/f7b5abc1475d61dce458eff4bad1824852d45c67/data-raw/adbc_connection.R#L15)
- [ ] Update the [test script](https://github.com/r-dbi/docker/blob/233bf5427594fd8b10c6fe65d6b5a1be347e0f38/compose_files/test/test-adbi.R#L6) in r-dbi/docker ourselves

The fabricQueryR package also uses adbi, but it passes a driver object and is unaffected.

## Deprecate

- [ ] Add the `.Deprecated()` warning, as in the first version of #60, but only when the package function returns an `adbc_driver`; any other result already falls through to the Driver Manager
- [ ] Remove the fallback

title: Required `rcc` check has failed on `main` since 2026-08-05, blocking all merges
description:
Every `rcc` run on `main` has failed since 2026-08-05 (62 runs as of 2026-09-23). The `main` ruleset requires `rcc`, so no pull request can be merged: #59, #60 and #69 all show it as failed.

There are three independent failures, none of them in package code:

| Failing job | Since | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Windows arm64 (`rcc: windows-11-arm (4.6)`) | 2026-08-05 | The job was added in 021c460 (cynkra/cynkratemplate#99) and has failed all 55 of its completed runs. There is no Windows arm64 binary of adbcdrivermanager, and the 0.24.0-3 source on CRAN does not compile with the aarch64 Rtools toolchain, because `strsafe.h` redefines functions that libc++'s `<cwchar>` expects. The fix, apache/arrow-adbc#4591, is merged upstream but not yet in a CRAN release. |
| macOS R 4.6 (`rcc: macos-latest (4.6)`) | 2026-09-20 | CRAN published some zstd-compressed macOS binaries for R 4.6 in September, which pak cannot extract (r-lib/pkgdepends#485, r-lib/pak#915). CRAN has since replaced them, but `mac.cran.dev`, which pak also downloads from, still serves the zstd copies, and pak does not check them against `PACKAGES` (r-lib/pkgcache#145). |
| Formatting suggestions on fork PRs (`format-suggest`) | 2026-09-13 | Commit d509c3c deleted `.github/workflows/style/action.yml`, but [`format-suggest.yaml`](https://github.com/r-dbi/adbi/blob/f23662b2f09dbb8ee342e81870af1859e12421b8/.github/workflows/format-suggest.yaml#L107) still points `uses:` at it. This one is not a required check. |

Rather than patch these one by one, the plan is to replace the CI with a small setup that lives in this repository. The current one is 19,825 lines in `.github/` plus 43 actions referenced from cynkra/cynkratemplate at `@main`. Of those lines, 18,570 are revdep tooling that has never run. The fledge workflow runs daily but cannot act, because `NEWS.md` is not fledge-managed. Changes to the template's `main` also reach this repository's CI without a commit here, as with cynkra/cynkratemplate@ecc1ea2 and cynkra/cynkratemplate@5a7c95b.

## Plan

One workflow, `rcc` (`.github/workflows/rcc.yaml`), on pushes to `main`, pull requests and manual runs. Like r-dbi/odbc, its jobs use the r-lib/actions steps directly:

- **Smoke** (`smoke`): Ubuntu, R release. Runs lintr, then roxygen2 8.1.0 followed by a check that the working tree is still clean, then R CMD check. All other jobs wait for it.
- **Check matrix** (`check`): Ubuntu with R devel, oldrel-1 and 4.1; macOS release; Windows release. R 4.1 is a fixed entry because it is the oldest version the test tooling supports (testthat requires R ≥ 4.1). While `mac.cran.dev` serves the stale zstd builds (see above), the macOS entry builds adbcdrivermanager and adbcsqlite from CRAN's sources, via `adbcdrivermanager=?source, adbcsqlite=?source` in `extra-packages`; that line goes once the mirror is fixed or the next ADBC release reaches CRAN.
- **Without suggested packages** (`suggests`): Only the hard dependencies plus testthat are installed, so tests must skip cleanly when DBItest, adbcsqlite and the other suggested packages are missing.
- **Coverage** (`coverage`): Runs covr and uploads the results to Codecov, which comments on coverage changes and never fails the build.
- **Website** (`pkgdown`): Built on pull requests, deployed to `gh-pages` from `main`.
- **Gate** (`rcc`): Passes only if all other jobs passed; this is the check the ruleset requires.

Everything else in `.github/` is removed: the auto-commits (formatting, docs, snapshots), fledge, the revdep workflows, `format-suggest`, `commit-suggest`, `R-CMD-check-status`, `R-CMD-check-dev`, lock-threads, ccache, clang-format, the arm64 jobs and all references to cynkra/cynkratemplate. From then on, this repository maintains its own CI rather than following the template, and CI changes go through pull requests here.

The same pull request also:

- Adds a `.lintr` that turns off the linters clashing with DBI's naming conventions, and fixes the remaining lints.
- Removes `air.toml` and `adbi.Rproj`, along with their entries (and those for ccache) in `.Rbuildignore` and `.gitignore`.
- Renames `codecov.yml` and `_pkgdown.yml` to `codecov.yaml` and `_pkgdown.yaml`, so every YAML file uses the same extension.
- Regenerates the documentation with roxygen2 8.1.0 from CRAN instead of the development version `8.1.0.9000`.
- Enables Codecov comments; the statuses stay informational.
- Raises `Depends` to `R (>= 4.1.0)`, the oldest version CI tests.
- Keeps the workflow token read-only except for the website deploy, and pins third-party actions to a SHA.

Once it is merged, #59, #60 and #69 need `main` merged in to pick up the new checks.

title: Allow database-specific SQL quoting
description:
adbi currently delegates identifier and string quoting to `DBI::ANSI()`.

This can generate invalid SQL for databases with different quoting rules. For example, BigQuery requires backticks for quoted identifiers:

```r
DBI::dbQuoteIdentifier(con, "table")
# Current:  "table"
# Expected: `table`
```

Unlike ODBC, which exposes the backend-specific identifier quote character through `SQL_IDENTIFIER_QUOTE_CHAR`, ADBC currently provides no equivalent metadata.

Could adbi allow the quoting behavior to be configured per connection, perhaps through a dialect or quoting callbacks?

For example, a BigQuery connection could use:

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(
  adbi::adbi(...),
  quote_identifier = function(x) {
    DBI::SQL(encodeString(x, quote = "`"), names = names(x))
  }
)
```

Related ADBC issues:

- apache/arrow-adbc#1395
- apache/arrow-adbc#1396
- apache/arrow-adbc#1398

title: "NOT_IMPLEMENTED" errors when using with `adbcflightsql`
description:
## Description

I see that the community has successfully been using `adbi` together with `adbcflightsql`, e.g. in references in issues #28 and #31. This opens up the very exciting possibility of using `dbplyr` with the remote database over FlightSQL. However, I'm having trouble getting this off the ground, perhaps some of some combination of versions? I have a server running a FlightSQL protocol, and I am able to connect to it and query it using `adbcdrivermanager` directory:

```
> db <- adbc_database_init(adbcflightsql::adbcflightsql(), uri  = "grpc+tcp://127.0.0.1:50056", username = "...", password = askpass())
> con |>
+     read_adbc("SELECT * from a") |>
+     tibble::as_tibble()
# A tibble: 25 × 2
       a   asq
   <dbl> <dbl>
... < edited out > ...
```

For the corresponding `adbi` based connection, I can connect and list tables:
```
> drv <- adbi::adbi("adbcflightsql")   # create an adbi driver instance
> con <- adbi::dbConnect(drv, uri  = "grpc+tcp://127.0.0.1:50056", username = "...", password = askpass())
> dbListTables(con)
 [1] "columns"         "df_settings"     "parameters"      "routines"        "schemata"        "tables"         
 [7] "views"           "a"
```
However, I get a `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error when I try to query a table:
```
> con |> dbGetQuery("SELECT * FROM a LIMIT 10")
Error in adbcdrivermanager::adbc_statement_get_parameter_schema(stmt) : 
  NOT_IMPLEMENTED: 
```

The server is a development project of mine and in its debug logs I can see that the last FlightSQL request made was a `do_action_create_prepared_statement`. I am not sure what is not implemented. My initial expectation was that some part of the FlightSQL protocol necessary isn't implemented on the server's part, but the fact that `adbcdrivermanager` works by itself and the debug logs is making
me look elsewhere now.A remaining possibility, of course, is that the server is returning data (ultimately, the last thing, a
`ActionCreatePreparedStatementResult`) that in some way fall outside what `adbi` supports currently.

## Questions

Is this a known limitation, or correctable setup mistake on my part? Or if not, is there debug logging I can enable to figure out more about what isn't implemented, or particular R functions where I could add breakpoints with `debug(...)` to learn more?

## Version info

Server / FlightSQL info from the `adbi` object:
```
  Vendor arrow version: 1.3
  Driver name: ADBC Flight SQL Driver - Go
  Driver version: (unknown or development build)
  Driver arrow version: v18.4.2-0.20251124222331-4b04248429bc
```

Client
* Rocky 8 operating system
* R 4.4.1
* `adbcdrivermanager` and `adbcflightsql` were tested first from the multiverse (0.21.0) and then dev versions from github (0.21.0.9000)
* `adbi` version 0.1.2
* `DBI` version 1.2.3

title: ArrowArrayInitFromSchema(): Error parsing schema->format: Expected decimal bitwidth of 128 or 256 but found 64
description:
Connecting using `adbi` and `adbcflightsql` against a Arrow Flight SQL Server and reading data from a decimal column ("lineitem" table) complains with the error message "ArrowArrayInitFromSchema(): Error parsing schema->format: Expected decimal bitwidth of 128 or 256 but found 64".

Replicate by running two Flight SQL Servers, using container images from **voltrondata/sqlflite** (older) and **gizmodata/gizmosql** (newer):

```bash
# first run this arrow flight sql server (arrow v 17 and duckdb v 1.1.1)
docker run --name sqlflite --detach --rm --tty --init --publish 31336:31337   --env TLS_ENABLED="0" --env SQLFLITE_PASSWORD="sqlflite_password"   --env PRINT_QUERIES="1" --env INIT_SQL_COMMANDS="SET threads = 1; SET memory_limit = '1GB';"   --pull missing voltrondata/sqlflite:latest

# then run the new "version" of this "gizmosql" (arrow v 20 and duckdb v 1.3)
docker run --name gizmosql --detach --rm --tty --init --publish 31337:31337   --env TLS_ENABLED="0" --env GIZMOSQL_PASSWORD="sqlflite_password"   --env PRINT_QUERIES="1" --env INIT_SQL_COMMANDS="SET threads = 1; SET memory_limit = '1GB';"   --pull missing gizmodata/gizmosql:latest
```

Then from R make a connection to the newer server:

```r

#install.packages("adbi")
#install.packages("adbcflightsql", repos = "https://community.r-multiverse.org")

con <- adbi::dbConnect(adbi::adbi("adbcflightsql"),
  uri = "grpc://127.0.0.1:31337/",
  username = "sqlflite_username",
  password = "sqlflite_password"
)

con |> DBI::dbGetQuery("select #5 from lineitem;")

# we get an error ! ArrowArrayInitFromSchema(): Error parsing schema->format: Expected decimal bitwidth of 128 or 256 but found 64


DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

Note that this works against the other (older) server

```r
# it works against the older version (voltrondata/sqlflite)

con <- adbi::dbConnect(adbi::adbi("adbcflightsql"),
  uri = "grpc://127.0.0.1:31336/",
  username = "sqlflite_username",
  password = "sqlflite_password"
)

con |> DBI::dbGetQuery("select #5 from lineitem;")

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

title: Example showing how to provide "flight call options" when making a connection against a (quackpy) Flight SQL server
description:
Trying to figure out how to use adbi to get a connection to a Flight SQL server and while [able to successfully get a connection against Voltron's `sqlflite` server - reproducable w containers here](https://github.com/KTH-Library/duckflight), I am stuck on authenticating against another containerized server [`quackpy`](https://github.com/quackscience/quackpy). 

From python the following can be used to establish a connection against the quackpy Flight SQL server:

```python
from pyarrow.flight import FlightClient, Ticket, FlightCallOptions 
sql="""SELECT version()"""  
flight_ticket = Ticket(sql)

token = (b"authorization", bytes(f"user:persistence".encode('utf-8')))
options = FlightCallOptions(headers=[token])
client = FlightClient(f"grpc://localhost:8815")
reader = client.do_get(flight_ticket, options)
arrow_table = reader.read_all()
```

From R, using adbi, how do I provide the equivalent "FlightCallOptions" when initiating the connection?

Attempting to provide authentication details through the uri (I might be doing this wrong obviously) I get a server response like below:
